items.item: All artwork applies the rule sheet's ink contours, translucent gouache, palette assignments and upper-left candlelight as one visual language.
Paper, wax and silver retain distinct material appearances wherever depicted, within the fixed painted treatment.
Each character remains recognizable across portraits and meetings, preserving recorded clothing, hair, visible accessory counts and house identity while allowing the required expression changes.
Venn uses the rust forked reed, Sere the blue three-reed mark and Orlan the plum stepped arch, associated with the correct named person.
Confidence and Disclosure depict the same recorded Reed Gallery and retain Mara at left, Ivo at centre and Tessa at right.
Every depicted P01 preserves the pendant sheet's silver oval, single top loop, right hinge and recognizable reed engraving; only its recorded Closed/Open state changes.
Readers and outcomes consistently implement the information map's counter labels, knowledge gating, reading behavior and input-action meanings.
Arrival and Confidence conceal the inscription, Disclosure reveals it, and Mara retains the pendant throughout.

requirementChecks.criteria: Read the original file properties: Format: presentation document; at least eight actual pages. Stage: final.

The sheet occupies one page and explicitly records parchment #F2E6CC, charcoal #252A30, Venn rust #8A4934, Sere blue #315B70 and Orlan plum #69445C. It specifies ink contours, translucent gouache, paper, wax, silver and candlelight from the upper left. Organization may vary; missing codes, incorrect assignments or omitted material and lighting instructions fail.

Compare the artwork with the rule sheet: contours read as ink, painted areas retain translucent gouache qualities, and illuminated forms receive candlelight from the upper left. Parchment, charcoal and house accents preserve their specified roles. Pigment texture and local shading may vary; a conflicting rendering style, house-color substitution or reversed lighting fails.

Read the register against 03-court-records.en.md. C01 is Mara Venn, 168 cm, Composed and Concerned; C02 is Ivo Sere, 182 cm, Reserved and Relieved; C03 is Tessa Orlan, 174 cm, Formal and Wary. Each entry includes its recorded position, house, skin, hair, clothing colors, accessories and counts. P01 records silver construction, 36 × 24 × 6 mm closed in height × width × thickness order, Ivo as owner, Mara as holder throughout both branches, the oval body, single top loop, right hinge, three-reed engraving with its middle-reed diagonal break, smooth back, and Closed/Open states with their interior visibility. Table or prose layouts are acceptable; missing or conflicting record fields fail.

Each named character has front, side and back standing views, both visibly differentiated and correctly named expressions, a portrait close-up and a small correspondence portrait. The sheet prints its correct record ID and height: Mara C01/168 cm, Ivo C02/182 cm, Tessa C03/174 cm. Check appearance and accessory counts against 03-court-records.en.md, including Mara's one low braid, brass pin and cream sash; Ivo's silver curls, silver pin and round spectacle frame; and Tessa's cropped hair, silver pin and cream belt. Panel order and pose details may vary; omitted views, mislabeled expressions or altered fixed features fail.

Read the delivered correspondence against the complete L01–L03 records. L01 belongs to Ivo Sere with the blue Sere mark, L02 to Tessa Orlan with the plum Orlan mark, and L03 to Mara Venn with the rust Venn mark. Each sheet includes an envelope and Arrival reader with the correct ID, subject, sender, recipient and full letter including salutation and signature; L03 identifies itself as Sent copy. Readers include the recorded title and actions, and L01 includes Leave the pendant closed and Open the pendant. Reflow across lines is allowed; omissions, rewritten correspondence, swapped marks, duplicated letters or missing recorded reader fields fail.

The sheet supplies all six requested representations and identifies P01, Ivo Sere as owner, Mara Venn as holder, and closed dimensions of 36 × 24 × 6 mm in height × width × thickness order. All views depict the same silver oval with one top loop, right-side hinge, three vertical cover reeds, diagonal break across the middle reed and smooth back. The open cover swings right and exposes Tessa ordered the gate opened. Closed and Open states are named. Enlarged detail and simplified icon rendering are allowed if defining features remain recognizable; missing views, changed construction or incorrect ownership fail.

The map accounts for L01, L02, L03, B01 and B02 and assigns each the content and actions in 04-letters-and-states.en.md. It records Arrival at Trust 1/Clues 0/P01 Closed; leaving the pendant closed leads to Confidence at 2/0/Closed, while opening it leads to Disclosure at 0/1/Open. Mara remains holder. The three characters' public identities, pendant ownership and possession are distinguished from the inscription and Tessa's gate order, which remain locked until Disclosure. Include the recorded dialogue and expression assignments, minimum text height, 200% vertical scrolling, contrast thresholds, and controller/touch prompt meanings and positions. Diagram or table structure may vary; missing screens, premature knowledge or incorrect transitions fail.

All three readers identify Arrival and show Trust 1 and Clues 0; L01 shows closed P01. Both input versions of Confidence show Trust 2, Clues 0 and closed P01, with Mara Composed, Ivo Relieved and Tessa Formal. Both Disclosure versions show Trust 0, Clues 1 and open P01, with Mara Concerned, Ivo Reserved and Tessa Wary. Outcome dialogue and speaker match the corresponding scene excerpt in 04-letters-and-states.en.md. Mara retains possession. Layout may vary within the required geometry; mixed branch values, wrong expressions, incorrect dialogue or transferred possession fail.

Inspect player-facing screen regions separately from explanatory sheet annotations. L01 and Confidence represent the protected inscription with a lock icon and Sealed; no Arrival or Confidence screen reveals the inscription or attributes the gate order to Tessa. Disclosure visibly reveals Tessa ordered the gate opened. Any other disabled action also combines the lock icon with Sealed. L02 and L03 need not introduce an inscription panel absent from their records. Early disclosure, missing required lock treatment or altered inscription text fails.

Judge embedded screens in normalized logical coordinates, independently of exported image pixel dimensions. Their layout follows the specified 16:9 logical canvas, with functional text and controls inside the 48-unit safe inset and default text at least 18 logical units high. Body text and ordinary controls meet 4.5:1 contrast; large text, icons and disabled controls meet 3:1. Scaled mockup presentation is allowed if the internal proportions and text sizes remain assessable. Content intruding into the safe inset, undersized text or insufficient contrast fails.

Each default reader positions its letter body at logical x 576, y 144 in a 960 × 648 reading rectangle. Count visible English line lengths including spaces; none exceeds 75 characters. A separate enlargement demonstrates text at 200% with readable reflow and visible vertical-scrolling affordance or continuation. The enlarged viewport may show only part of the complete letter. A zoom label alone, horizontal scrolling, clipped text without scrolling or an incorrect default column fails.

Each sheet contains two versions of its outcome with identical state, dialogue, knowledge and Return to hall behavior. The action occupies the lower-right logical area x 1488, y 912, width 336, height 72. The controller version shows a south-face-button symbol and the touch version a fingertip symbol. Input-specific prompt styling may differ; missing variants, incorrect symbols, displaced actions or changed narrative outcomes fail.

Match each correspondence portrait and branch character to its character sheet and the fixed court record. Preserve skin tone, hairstyle, house clothing colors, visible accessories and mark geometry; ensure house marks identify the correct named correspondent. Expression changes must follow the state records. Cropping and reduced detail at portrait scale are acceptable when identity remains clear; added accessories, swapped house identities or incompatible character designs fail.

Both outcomes visibly take place in the recorded Reed Gallery: a long passage with three shallow arched recesses, pale limewashed plaster, a dark timber bench, an unglazed terracotta floor and a candle niche at the upper left of the meeting composition. Mara stands at left, Ivo at centre and Tessa at right in both input versions. Outcome expressions and pendant state may change; a different room, missing defining setting features or reversed character arrangement fails.

Review the complete 10-second sequence against the timing record: 0–3 seconds shows the L01 Arrival reader at Trust 1/Clues 0 with closed P01; 3–6 seconds selects Open the pendant and swings the cover right as the inscription enters view; 6–10 seconds shows B02 Disclosure at Trust 0/Clues 1 with open P01, the exact inscription, recorded Disclosure dialogue and Concerned/Reserved/Wary expressions for Mara/Ivo/Tessa. Preserve the supplied character and pendant identities, house colors and marks, upper-left light and Mara's possession. Editing and camera movement may vary within those phases; incorrect timing, early revelation, missing selection or inconsistent final state fails.
requirementChecks.manualReason: Inspect complete SHA-bound original outputs. This source draft contains no completed professional or model-output review; partial-frame/page sampling cannot prove whole-output compliance.

requirementChecks.criteria: Count at least eight pages and read Confidence and Disclosure on the opening page. The explanation connects each L01 choice to its correct outcome, counters, pendant state, expression assignments and inscription visibility, retaining Ivo's ownership and Mara's possession. Artwork is placed beside the relevant implemented rule, record ID or branch state rather than presented without explanatory linkage. Page order after the opening may vary; missing branch explanations, incorrect state facts or unassociated artwork fails.

Read the presentation's stated specifications and reproduced record material. It repeats P01, 36 × 24 × 6 mm, Ivo Sere as owner and Mara Venn as holder. Character depictions preserve the recorded clothing colors, accessory counts and house marks. It also repeats all five art-rule codes, #F2E6CC, #252A30, #8A4934, #315B70 and #69445C, and explicitly identifies upper-left candlelight. Specifications may appear in captions, tables or legible reused sheets; absent required facts or contradictions fail.

The document has identifiable sections labeled Player-visible facts and Author notes. Public identities, the loan and Mara's possession are distinguished from concealed evidence and the gate-order attribution. Player knowledge is qualified by Arrival, Confidence or Disclosure so that an author-only fact is not represented as known before revelation. Sections may share a page if clearly separated; unlabeled mixing or premature player knowledge fails.

Find recognizable, legible reused material from every listed source, including stills that correspond to the delivered sequence. Reused artwork is accompanied by the applicable rules, record IDs or branch states. Crops and scale changes are acceptable when the source and implemented requirement remain identifiable; text-only mentions, unrelated replacements, unreadable thumbnails or an omitted source fail.

All artwork applies the rule sheet's ink contours, translucent gouache, palette assignments and upper-left candlelight as one visual language. Paper, wax and silver retain distinct material appearances wherever depicted, within the fixed painted treatment.

Each character remains recognizable across portraits and meetings, preserving recorded clothing, hair, visible accessory counts and house identity while allowing the required expression changes. Venn uses the rust forked reed, Sere the blue three-reed mark and Orlan the plum stepped arch, associated with the correct named person. Confidence and Disclosure depict the same recorded Reed Gallery and retain Mara at left, Ivo at centre and Tessa at right.

Every depicted P01 preserves the pendant sheet's silver oval, single top loop, right hinge and recognizable reed engraving; only its recorded Closed/Open state changes. Readers and outcomes consistently implement the information map's counter labels, knowledge gating, reading behavior and input-action meanings. Arrival and Confidence conceal the inscription, Disclosure reveals it, and Mara retains the pendant throughout.
